div.head: ECf 32 A 12
div.ab: Uniuersi uero predicti singulis annis in crastino Purificationis beate Marie debent omni excusatione remota arma sua per uniuersum regnum ostendere, scilicet in ciuitatibus regni et in burgis et in castellis et in hundredis et in wapentachiis regni, secundum quod eis statutum est et adiudicatum, et iuxta quod debent; et iccirco hoc fieri debet uno eodem die per uniuersum regnum, ut predictum est, ne aliqui possint arma sua familiaribus suis et notis accommodare nec ipsi illa mutuo accipere ac iusticiam domini regis defraudare et dominum regem et regnum offendere.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 656 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

note.seg: vor Reiserichtern ward in den Grafschaften das Waffenhalten beschworen nach jener Assisa von 1181
in the shires the keeping of arms was sworn before itinerant justices, according to that Assize of 1181

vgl. Rot. pat. I 72 a. 1207: si aliquis fraudulenter amouerit catalla sua gegen Steuereinschätzung. Vielleicht birgt der Londoner hier die Spur eines verlorenen Gesetzes gegen Vorweisen von Waffen als eigen, die nur entliehen waren

cf. Rot. pat. I 72 a. 1207: si aliquis fraudulenter amouerit catalla sua, against tax assessment. Perhaps the Londoner here preserves the trace of a lost law against showing as one’s own arms that were only borrowed

div.ab: And all the aforesaid must every year, on the morrow of the Purification of blessed Mary, setting aside every excuse, show their arms throughout the whole kingdom, namely in the cities of the kingdom and in the boroughs and in the castles and in the hundreds and in the wapentakes of the kingdom, according as has been decreed and adjudged for them, and according as they ought; and therefore this must be done on one and the same day throughout the whole kingdom, as was said before, so that none may lend their arms to their household and acquaintances, nor themselves receive them on loan, and so defraud the justice of the lord king and offend the lord king and the kingdom.
